notes: Lead: CTO Gabrielle Ortiz. Use-case: agent-facing live suggestions + automatic tool-calling to CRM for status updates and ticket enrichment. Primary technical ask: reliable RAG with provenance (exact citation + source timestamp) across Zendesk, internal Confluence docs, and archived call transcripts in S3. Latency target: 150-250ms for agent suggestion path (critical); background summarization can be relaxed. Burst requirement: up to 1200 reqs/min in morning peaks; need graceful degradation + canary routing during spikes. POC scope: 2-week run in staging to validate: (1) citation precision & source attribution, (2) freshness (TTL and near-real-time updates from Confluence), (3) multi-source retriever ranking and blending, (4) tool-calling reliability for ticket updates. Cost sensitivity: moderate — willing to consider Dedicated for SLOs if unit economics and observability are solid. Security must-haves: KMS integration, SOC2 evidence, SSO/SAML, audit logging, and documented data residency. Quote from CTO: "If citations can't be traced back to a single source with a timestamp we won't trust it." POC blockers: legal wants data-residency clause in contract; engineering needs a private/int8 quantized runtime for on-prem eval; product wants sample dashboards showing per-route token cost and citation accuracy. Next actions for Redwood: deliver ingestion runbook for multi-source connectors, provide canary routing config for spike handling, produce sample RAG freshness runbook, and hand over a short checklist for audit compliance. Stakeholders: Gabrielle Ortiz (CTO), Priya Menon (Head of Ops), Marcus Lin (SRE), Maya Chen (AE).
short_summary: Enterprise CCaaS vendor evaluating Redwood for RAG-backed agent assist and ticket workflows. Focus: citation provenance, freshness, multi-source retrievers, and reliability during traffic spikes. POC underway; legal/quantization are current blockers.
